newsitem.title: USA: Phila. woman files suit against stock tax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Phila. woman files suit against stock tax - paper.

text.p: A Philadelphia woman has filed suit against the city challenging the constitutionality of its personal property tax, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.
The suit, filed by Allison Moore, asks that the city be required to refund money collected from the tax, which is levied primarily against stock holdings in out-of-state companies.

Philadelphia collects about $16 million annually from the tax, which has already been ruled unconstitutional by the state's Commonwealth Court. That decision is being appealed to the state Supreme Court, but most local governments have already scrapped the tax on the expectation that it would be rejected by the court.

Philadelphia has enacted a bill designed to keep the tax in place in a different form if the state Supreme Court kills the existing levy. Moore's lawsuit seeks a ruling declaring that proposal invalid as well, the newspaper said.
Several local banks have begun moving operations to outlying suburbs in an attempt to avoid the tax. Bank officials are meeting with the city to find a compromise.
